implementation.summary: D37 audited and exercised the existing P14 recovery and Helm paths on an exact clean candidate. No production code change was justified: local appliance backup/restore, Docker acceptance and Helm upgrade/rollback/restart already provide the bounded implementation under test. The Floci provider lane was attempted with its required toolchain and is recorded as blocked after reproducible apply timeouts.

security_and_recovery.journey: The real Docker journey reaches health, executes worker/restart/replay/cancel flows and restores PostgreSQL rows plus /var/lib/ronin artifacts/evidence after destructive mutation. The real Helm journey installs an isolated single-replica release, confines a synthetic token to a Secret, upgrades to revision 2, rolls back to revision 1, verifies health/API, restarts the deployment and confirms the same queued job ID survives.
security_and_recovery.negative_paths: Candidate contracts cover rejected Compose exposure, malformed/unsafe backup manifests, invalid migration states, backup checksum/inventory barriers and Docker qualification fail-closed rules. Helm verifies the Secret boundary and public single-node values. The provider lane is retained as a negative result because apply did not complete.
security_and_recovery.provider_scope: Docker used PostgreSQL 16.4, Floci/S3 and Azurite/Azure real local services. Helm used kind and the pinned local Ronin image. Floci/Terraform 1.13.5 was attempted against digest-pinned Floci 2.1.0 but apply timed out twice; this does not certify external object-store backup/recovery.

limitations: The strict Docker and Helm acceptances were run from the clean Git checkout at the exact candidate SHA because the runners require Git metadata; their source identity, image digest and evidence paths are recorded explicitly. The archive sandbox separately passed its P14 and Helm contract selections.

Floci/Terraform qualification is a real attempted provider lane, not a skip: plan and validation passed, apply timed out at both configured limits, and the runner verified destroy/state/resource cleanup. No provider PASS is claimed.
The exact candidate archive has no @playwright/test, so browser execution is SKIP and is not counted as PASS. No hosted workflow or GitHub Actions evidence was used.
